launch_binding.reason: scr_init and the first prompt are both owned by the native REPL; no Lisp code can execute between them without a minimal native launch seam

screen_contract.color: screen-put-char/screen-write-string attribute 15; no direct color-RAM poke
screen_contract.separator: screen-write-string colors columns 1..66, then poke writes raw screen code 64 to 0x09e1..0x0a22

visual_oracle.note: The independent oracle duplicates the normative run stream and checks the executed screen operations, raw separator bytes and prompt advance. A real-hardware screenshot remains mandatory before wave sealing.

bank.attribution: The generated launch seam alone overflowed the c356 overlay ceiling. Narrowing bounded REPL cursor/status values from int to uint8_t and removing the two unused buffer bytes more than pays for the seam; REPL_BUF_MAX is permanently gated to 2..255.

directory.reason: The two entries cross the next eight-entry boot alignment boundary.

boot_overlay.attribution: No boot-overlay-owned source changed. The REPL correction moves the overlay VMA from c354 to c304, so its absolute relocations change while size and control-audit structure remain unchanged.

resident_external_image.accounting_note: Only the 351 code bytes remain in EXT after boot. Banner metadata is reclaimed after installation and does not reduce post-composition EXT headroom.

spec_findings_requiring_owner_resolution: The original 150..200-byte blob estimate is exceeded: the smallest measured contract-faithful implementation retains 351 code bytes.
The native REPL owns scr_init and the first prompt, so the requirement of a purely Lisp startup is replaced by a generated-ordinal launch seam.
The prose art and explicit coordinate list disagree; the probe treats the explicit coordinate list as normative.
The actual visible write count is 235, not roughly 180, when the 66-cell separator and 22-cell subtitle are counted.
The current screen character mapper has no established middle-dot mapping; the probe uses the visible ASCII subtitle WORKBENCH - DIALECT V2 instead of guessing a glyph.
The boot overlay remains size-neutral but is not byte-identical because the separately attributable REPL correction rebases it.
